correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian product moments give a covariance map with a positive symmetric 2-by-2 block and a strictly smaller antisymmetric eigenvalue. Its Perron eigenvalue yields the explicit radius and unique frontier, with both endpoint limits verified by asymptotic expansions. The underlying SDE stability comparison follows from its exact covariance drift. The embedded program checked 185 direct matrix identities and numerical boundaries; finite checks supplement rather than substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating source gives positivity and finite-time estimates, not the sharp two-site long-time mean-square threshold. The 2024 full-text method does not prove this exact noise/step frontier. Semantic published-finding corpus comparisons found no claim that entails the stated coupling-dependent covariance eigenvalue equation and its two distinct asymptotic limits. Classical Gaussian lognormal second moments are not claimed as novel. Residual risks are explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An equivalent two-site covariance calculation in older stochastic-numerics or Markov-switching literature might exist outside inspected full texts.
The 2022 Yang--Yang--Zhang full text on almost-sure stability was unavailable; the distinction in discretization/stability type reduces, but does not eliminate, possible overlap.
The symmetric two-site and independent equal-noise assumptions limit extrapolation to general finite-element discretizations.

value.rationale: The result quantifies a practically relevant boundary between positivity preservation and long-time mean-square stability for the simplest coupled stochastic-heat FEM system. The gap between the semidiscrete SDE cutoff and large-step numerical cutoff is nonzero for every 0<b<a, and the exact formula supplies a sharp stability regression benchmark. It is not a mere numerical one-off or a generic textbook scalar test.
